key_insight: OnTrack streams step-by-step optimal transport monitoring to detect when an LLM agent trajectory diverges from successful references, enabling near-real-time alerts or aborts before costly bad actions accumulate.
engineering_relevance: It offers a low-latency safety layer for autonomous agents in operational settings like software repair, IT triage, and trading, where preventing irreversible failures matters more than post-hoc analysis.
method: Compares live agent steps and dependency structure to prior successful runs using structure-aware optimal transport.
Operates in three access regimes: full references, tool schemas only, or only generated step logs.
Triggers interventions in about a millisecond per step to alert users or block execution.
evidence_signal: On SWE-bench trajectories, using the first 8 steps improved failure-vs-success ranking by +0.057 AUROC over content similarity, and an abort policy saved about 18% compute with 5 of 6 aborts correctly stopping failing runs.
watch_item: Monitoring quality drops when historical reference data and tool/schema access are limited, so deployment should account for higher false alarms or weaker detection in sparse-data settings.
paper_title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport
